## 59c1ad6d4a45

**Reproduced semantic coverage gap: production never emits multiple seeds in one frame, although canonical frames do.** Canonical train example 0 has seed counts `[2, 1]` across its two frames. A census of 1,000 generated boards (250 for each of default/easy/medium/hard) from generator SHA-256 `b9549d13a8ab818c7d77d8fc0b0d335b835ba6c8509d4f90c1d75c722c09e4b9` observed 1,492 frames, all with exactly one seed.

A plausible rival therefore processes only the first row-major red seed in each frame. On canonical train example 0 it differs from the intended rule at `(9,4)`: the Racket rule paints that cell `8`, while the one-seed rival leaves it `0`. The supported apply command executed rule hash `caf3ed5492eb`; the exact input, Racket output, rival output, census, hashes, and disagreement are in `checks/audit/59c1ad6d4a45/`. This is a generated-domain teaching gap; the canonical input passes the canonical authority, but it is outside the selected generator's documented one-seed-per-frame invariant. I left the audit target unchanged.
